title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 168 (Right of finder of goods)

content.overview: Section 168 provides that the finder of goods has no right to sue the owner for compensation for trouble and expense voluntarily incurred by him to preserve the goods and to find out the owner; but he may retain the goods against the owner until he receives such compensation; and where the owner has offered a specific reward for the return of goods lost, the finder may sue for such reward, and may retain the goods until he receives it.
content.glance: Finder has no right to sue for voluntary expenses but may retain the goods until compensated; if a specific reward was offered, he may sue for it and retain until paid.
content.study: The finder of goods has no right to sue the owner for compensation for trouble and expense voluntarily incurred by him to preserve the goods and to find out the owner; but he may retain the goods against the owner until he receives such compensation; and where the owner has offered a specific reward for the return of goods lost, the finder may sue for such reward, and may retain the goods until he receives it. Current-law framing: limited rights of retainer and, where offered, claim for specific reward.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: The finder of goods has no right to sue the owner for compensation for trouble and expense voluntarily incurred by him to preserve the goods and to find out the owner; but he may retain the goods against the owner until he receives such compensation; and where the owner has offered a specific reward for the return of goods lost, the finder may sue for such reward, and may retain the goods until he receives it.

examples.title: Finder's retainer
examples.body: Finder incurs voluntary expenses. He cannot sue for them but may retain the goods until compensated. If a specific reward was offered, he may sue for the reward and retain until paid.

hypotheticals.question: Finder incurs expenses finding the owner. Can he sue for compensation?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 168 provides no right to sue for voluntary trouble and expense, but he may retain the goods until compensated. If a specific reward was offered, he may sue for that reward.
